# Lab 9.5: Serverless Spark in BigQuery Notebooks

## What We Are Going to Do
Start a serverless Spark session (Managed Service for Apache Spark) from a BigQuery notebook and read and write BigQuery tables with PySpark.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Enable the API and allow the session to use the network.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud services enable dataproc.googleapis.com
gcloud compute networks subnets update default --region=us-central1 --enable-private-ip-google-access</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[Console] Start from the template.** In Studio click **+ → Notebook → Notebook gallery** and open the **Apache Spark** starter. It contains the current import and session code. The core lines are:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • PYTHON
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">from google.cloud.dataproc_spark_connect import DataprocSparkSession
spark = DataprocSparkSession.builder.appName("lab09-spark").getOrCreate()</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The first session takes about a minute to start.

3. **[Console] Read a BigQuery table with Spark.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • PYTHON
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">df = spark.read.format("bigquery").load("bigquery-public-data.samples.shakespeare")
df.groupBy("corpus").sum("word_count").orderBy("sum(word_count)", ascending=False).show(5)</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Write back to BigQuery.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • PYTHON
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">from pyspark.sql import functions as F
out = df.groupBy("word").agg(F.sum("word_count").alias("total")).filter("total &gt; 1000")
out.write.format("bigquery").option("writeMethod", "direct").mode("overwrite").save("lab09.spark_common_words")</span>
</code></pre>
</div>

<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">spark.stop()</span>
</code></pre>

<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud dataproc sessions list --location=us-central1

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Session | Serverless, no cluster to create |
| Read / write | Spark BigQuery connector |
| When to use Spark | Complex Python logic or existing Spark code |
| Cost | Billed while the session runs, so stop it |
